title: System.Text.Json
description: A high-performance JSON serializer built into .NET, optimized for speed and low allocations.

data.text: System.Text.Json is the built-in JSON serializer for .NET. It is designed for high performance, low allocations, and security, making it the preferred choice for modern .NET applications.

data.title: Custom Options

terms.definition: The main class for JSON serialization and deserialization.
Provides options to customize serialization behavior.

data.title: Performance
data.text: System.Text.Json is typically 2-3x faster than Newtonsoft.Json with lower memory allocations.

`System.Text.Json` is the built-in serializer. Options control naming policy, null handling, casing, and reference loops, and attributes such as `[JsonPropertyName]` and `[JsonIgnore]` shape individual members. It is also source-generatable, which removes reflection at startup and trims the dependency graph for AOT.

data.title: Configured options and source generation
System.Text.Json vs Newtonsoft.Json
data.text: System.Text.Json is faster and built in, and it is the default for ASP.NET Core. Newtonsoft.Json still wins on a few behaviors that migrated projects relied on — `JsonConvert` with more flexible converter discovery and some legacy patterns. For new code, start with System.Text.Json and reach for Newtonsoft only when a specific feature is genuinely missing.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Built into .NET, no extra package needed
data.takeaway: System.Text.Json is the default choice for JSON in modern .NET.
